question.text: Saraswati Capital AIF is valuing investee company Kavach Defence. Year-5 FCF is INR 120 crore; post-Year-5 perpetual growth 'g' = 4%; WACC = 12%. Using the Gordon Growth formula, what is the undiscounted Terminal Value at end of Year 5?

explanation.text: The Logic: TV = FCF(T+1) / (WACC - g) = [120 x (1+0.04)] / (0.12 - 0.04) = 124.8 / 0.08 = INR 1,560 crore. Per Section 14.6, FCF(T+1) must be grown by (1+g) first before dividing by (WACC - g). The Trap: INR 1,500 cr ignores the (1+g) growth on Year-5 FCF. INR 1,000 cr uses WACC alone (no perpetuity-with-growth). INR 1,250 cr double-applies growth. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) also tests the Gordon model, but with dividend-paying listed stocks (DDM). XIX-C applies it to FCFF of unlisted investees, where terminal value often dominates 60-80% of enterprise value. Manager's Pro-Tip: Do a sensitivity grid on 'g' in every IC memo: a 1% shift from 3% to 4% on the same WACC can swing TV by 20%+. LPAC members will challenge your terminal assumption before your explicit-period FCF.
